title: The Finite Simple Group Classification Landscape

items.title: Simple groups as composition factors
items.claim: Jordan–Hölder makes composition factors invariant but does not reconstruct extension data.

items.title: Quasisimple groups, components, and the layer
items.claim: Quasisimple means perfect with simple central quotient; components are subnormal quasisimple subgroups and E(G) is generated by them.

items.title: Distinct components commute
items.claim: Distinct components of a finite group commute.

items.title: The generalized Fitting subgroup
items.claim: For finite G, F*(G)=F(G)E(G).

items.title: The generalized Fitting subgroup contains its centralizer
items.claim: For finite G, C_G(F*(G))≤F*(G).

items.title: p-local subgroup
items.claim: A p-local subgroup is N_G(P) for a nontrivial p-subgroup P of G.

items.title: Cyclic and alternating simple families
items.claim: The elementary finite-simple entries are cyclic groups of prime order and A_n for n≥5.

items.title: Finite simple groups of Lie type as named families
items.claim: Use the source table’s classical, exceptional, twisted, and Suzuki–Ree names without developing Lie algebras.

items.title: The twenty-six sporadic simple groups
items.claim: The 26 sporadics are named exactly by the source table, with no construction or asserted pattern.

items.title: Classification of finite simple groups
items.claim: Every finite simple group is cyclic of prime order, alternating of degree at least five, of Lie type, or one of 26 sporadics, with standard low-rank identifications.

items.title: Low-rank coincidences and duplicate names
items.claim: Low-rank isomorphisms and exceptional parameter values are governed by the source table.

items.title: History of the first-generation classification
items.claim: The first-generation classification was a multi-decade programme distributed across the literature.

items.title: The quasithin gap and its repair
items.claim: The original programme required the Aschbacher–Smith quasithin classification to close a documented gap.

items.title: Status of the second-generation proof
items.claim: At the task’s 2026-08-14 design check, the GLS revision remained ongoing; the official Number 10 description states an aim to provide a complete proof, not completion.

items.title: Feit–Thompson odd-order theorem
items.claim: Every nontrivial finite group of odd order is solvable.

items.title: Schreier’s conjecture as a CFSG consequence
items.claim: Outer automorphism groups of finite simple groups are solvable.

items.title: Two-generation of finite simple groups
items.claim: Every finite simple group is generated by two elements, as a CFSG-dependent result.

items.title: What the library proves and does not prove about CFSG
items.claim: The library proves elementary family results and the local generalized-Fitting theorem, but not classification, recognition, order formulae, character tables, or sporadic constructions.

items.title: CFSG says every finite group is simple
items.claim: False: CFSG classifies finite simple groups; it does not make all finite groups simple.

items.title: Composition factors determine the finite group
items.claim: False: composition factors do not determine extension data.

items.title: All finite simple groups are alternating or cyclic
items.claim: False: Lie-type and sporadic entries remain.

items.title: The library proves CFSG
items.claim: False: CFSG is an external landmark, not a local proof.

items.title: The second-generation CFSG proof is complete as of 2026
items.claim: False: the dated source record describes an ongoing programme.

items.title: Lie type is developed here through Lie algebras
items.claim: False: this page gives table-level names only.

title: The Finite Simple Group Classification Landscape — Examples

items.title: Cyclic simple groups of prime order
items.claim: C_p is finite simple for prime p.

items.title: A5 as the smallest nonabelian simple group
items.claim: A5 is the smallest nonabelian finite simple group.

items.title: PSL(2,7) and a low-rank family entry
items.claim: PSL(2,7) is a sourced Lie-type entry under the table’s low-rank convention.

items.title: A Suzuki group family entry
items.claim: Suzuki groups occur in the source’s nonclassical twisted row.

items.title: The Mathieu groups among the sporadics
items.claim: M11, M12, M22, M23, and M24 are Mathieu entries in the sporadic list.

items.title: Composition factors do not determine the extension
items.claim: C4 and C2×C2 share composition factors but are not isomorphic.

title: Schur Multipliers and Universal Central Extensions

items.title: Schur multiplier
items.claim: M(G)=H_2(G;Z), not H²(G,C×) by definition.

items.title: Free-presentation kernel data
items.claim: A free presentation is 1→R→F→G→1 with F free and R normal.

items.title: Every finite group is finitely presented
items.claim: Every finite group has finitely many generators and relators.

items.title: The Hopf-formula quotient exists
items.claim: [F,R] is normal and contained in R∩[F,F].

items.title: Hopf-formula quotient
items.claim: The Hopf quotient is (R∩[F,F])/[F,R].

items.title: Low-degree sequence of a free presentation
items.claim: For 1→R→F→G→1 with F free: 0→H_2(G;Z)→R/[F,R]→F_ab→G_ab→0.

items.title: Hopf formula for the Schur multiplier
items.claim: For G=F/R with F free, M(G)≅(R∩[F,F])/[F,R].

items.title: Hopf formula is presentation-independent
items.claim: Hopf’s quotient is independent of the free presentation through M(G).

items.title: Multiplier of a finitely presented group
items.claim: A finitely presented group has finitely generated Schur multiplier.

items.title: Multiplier of a free group
items.claim: M(F)=0 for F free.

items.title: Multiplier of a cyclic group
items.claim: M(C)=0 for every cyclic group C.

items.title: Exterior square
items.claim: ∧²A=(A⊗_Z A)/⟨a⊗a:a∈A⟩.

items.title: Alternating universal property
items.claim: Alternating bilinear maps A×A→B factor uniquely through ∧²A.

items.title: Multiplier of an abelian group
items.claim: M(A)≅∧²A naturally for A abelian.

items.title: Central and stem extensions
items.claim: Central means K≤Z(E); stem means K≤Z(E)∩[E,E].

items.title: Perfect group
items.claim: G is perfect if G=[G,G], equivalently G_ab=0.

items.title: Universal central extension
items.claim: A universal central extension is initial among central extensions of G over G.

items.title: Uniqueness of universal central extensions
items.claim: A universal central extension is unique up to unique isomorphism over G.

items.title: Existence criterion for universal central extensions
items.claim: G admits a universal central extension iff G is perfect.

items.title: Free-presentation universal extension
items.claim: For perfect G=F/R, [F,F]/[F,R]→G is the universal-extension candidate.

items.title: Free-presentation construction is central
items.claim: For perfect G, [F,F]/[F,R]→G is central.

items.title: Free-presentation construction is universal
items.claim: For perfect G, [F,F]/[F,R]→G is universal.

items.title: Kernel of the universal central extension
items.claim: For perfect G, the universal-central-extension kernel is M(G).

items.title: Superperfect group
items.claim: Superperfect means H_1(G;Z)=H_2(G;Z)=0.

items.title: Universal central extension groups are superperfect
items.claim: The total group of a universal central extension is superperfect.

items.title: Universal coefficients in degree two
items.claim: For trivial A: 0→Ext¹_Z(G_ab,A)→H²(G;A)→Hom(M(G),A)→0 naturally; its splitting is noncanonical.

items.title: Central extensions of perfect groups
items.claim: For perfect G, central extensions by A are controlled by Hom(M(G),A).

items.title: Positive-degree homology of a finite group is order-torsion
items.claim: For finite G and n>0, |G| annihilates H_n(G;Z).

items.title: Multiplier of a finite group is finite
items.claim: For finite G, M(G) is finite abelian.

items.title: Schur covering group
items.claim: For finite G, a Schur cover is a stem extension with kernel isomorphic to M(G).

items.title: Existence of Schur covering groups
items.claim: Every finite group has a Schur covering group.

items.title: Projective representations and the multiplier
items.claim: Projective factor sets connect to M(G), but K× factor-set theory is intentionally outside this page.

items.title: Multiplier defined as H²(G,C×)
items.claim: False: M(G)=H_2(G;Z); H²(G,C×) is a qualified finite-group alternative.

items.title: Hopf formula is obviously independent
items.claim: False: independence follows through its identification with M(G).

items.title: Every group has a universal central extension
items.claim: False: precisely the perfect groups do.

items.title: Every central extension is stem
items.claim: False: stemness additionally puts the kernel in [E,E].

items.title: All finite Schur covers are unique
items.claim: False: general existence does not yield general uniqueness.

items.title: Universal coefficients split naturally
items.claim: False: the splitting is noncanonical.

title: Schur Multipliers and Universal Central Extensions — Examples

items.title: Multiplier of a cyclic group
items.claim: M(C)=0 for every cyclic C.

items.title: Multiplier of a finite abelian group
items.claim: For A≅C_n1×···×C_nr, M(A) is the corresponding exterior-square/pairwise-tensor sum.

items.title: Binary icosahedral cover of A5
items.claim: SL(2,5)→PSL(2,5)≅A5 is the sourced binary-icosahedral universal-cover example.

items.title: Hopf formula from a one-relator presentation
items.claim: For ⟨x | x^n⟩, Hopf’s quotient is trivial.

items.title: A stem extension that is not universal
items.claim: A sourced stem extension with nonperfect base is not universal.

items.title: Nonuniqueness of Schur covers
items.claim: A sourced finite group with nonisomorphic Schur covers refutes general uniqueness.
